title: A major asymmetric ice trap in a planet-forming disk. I. Formaldehyde and methanol
question: Search the asymmetric Oph IRS 48 dust trap for H2CO and CH3OH line emission to study complex organic chemistry in a pebble-concentrated environment.

data.sensitivity: 1.2 mJy beam^-1 channel^-1; integrated flux noise ~20 mJy km s^-1

evidence.quote: The 13 CO data are taken from van der Marel et al. (2016) and imaged using uvtapering for a similar beam size as the Band 7 data presented here.

what.value: High resolution (0.18x0.14") Band 7 continuum image used to determine emitting area

evidence.quote: the emitting area is determined using the high resolution (0.18×0.14") Band 7 continuum image (Francis & van der Marel 2020, and Figure A.3)

what.value: Integrated flux of the H2CO 9_{1,8}-8_{1,7} transition used as a lower limit in the rotational diagram

evidence.quote: The integrated flux of the H 2 CO 9 1,8 -8 1,7 transition from van der Marel et al. (2014) is included as a lower limit.

what.value: Gas surface density at 60 au (N_H2 ~ 1.6e22 cm^-2, or 0.07 g cm^-2) and gas disk mass of 0.6 M_Jup

evidence.quote: The gas surface density derived by van der Marel et al. (2016) at 60 au radius corresponds to N H 2 ∼ 1.6 · 10 22 cm −2, so the relative abundances of H 2 CO and CH 3 OH are ∼ 10 −8 w.r.t. H 2, consistent with previous estimates by van der Marel et al. (2014).
This is well above the gas surface density of 0.07 g cm −2 derived from CO isotopologues and DALI modelling by van der Marel et al. (2016), implying a dust-to-gas ratio ≫1.

what.value: Dust surface density of 2-8 g cm^-2 at the dust trap radius

evidence.quote: Ohashi et al. (2020) derived a dust surface density as high as 28 g cm −2 at the dust trap radius based on polarization continuum measurements and constraints from the centimeter emission in IRS 48.

As Ohashi et al. (2020) derived a much higher dust surface density of Σ d ∼2-8 g cm −2, we explore the effect of the dust surface density on the radial and vertical temperature structure, using Σ d ∼0.05, 0.5 and 5.0 g cm −2 between 60 and 80 au.

what.value: Disk position angle of 100 deg, inclination of 50 deg, and H2 densities of 10^6-10^8 cm^-3

evidence.quote: The profiles are extracted by deprojecting the zero-moment maps assuming a position angle of 100 ◦ and an inclination of 50 ◦ (Bruderer et al. 2014).
The H 2 densities in the midplane and molecular layers of IRS 48 are ∼ 10 6−8 cm −3 (Bruderer et al. 2014).

what.value: 19 um VISIR data tracing the um-sized grain distribution

evidence.quote: The µm-sized grain distribution as traced by 19 µm VISIR data (Geers et al. 2007) is indicated in the continuum image.

recipe.method: Subtract continuum in uv-plane using uvcontsub with a first-order polynomial, then identify H2CO and CH3OH transitions using the matched-filter technique.

recipe.goal: Line imaging, spectral extraction, and moment map creation
recipe.method: Image lines with tclean using natural weighting (and Briggs robust=0.5 for brightest lines). Extract integrated spectra and create zero- and first-moment maps using Keplerian masking; integrate spectra over velocity profiles (-2 to 12 km s^-1) to measure disk-integrated fluxes.
key_parameters: Keplerian mask parameters: d=135 pc, i=50 deg, M*=2.0 M_sun, v_source=4.55 km s^-1
Shared flux of blended p-H2CO 5_{4,2}-4_{4,1} and 5_{4,1}-4_{4,0} divided by 2
assumptions: Equal flux contribution for blended p-H2CO 5_{4,2}-4_{4,1} and 5_{4,1}-4_{4,0} transitions

recipe.goal: Deproject maps and extract radial and azimuthal intensity profiles
recipe.method: Deproject zero-moment maps and extract radial and azimuthal profiles for H2CO, CH3OH, continuum, and uv-tapered 13CO 6-5.
key_parameters: Azimuthal profile at r = 62 au (width 60 au), radial profile at phi = 192 deg E of N (width 100 deg); for 13CO, r = 35 au and phi = 269 deg

recipe.goal: Rotational diagram analysis to derive column densities, rotational temperatures, and abundances
recipe.method: Estimate emitting area from high-resolution Band 7 continuum, calculate upper state column densities Nu and optical depths following Loomis et al. (2018), and fit rotational diagrams using emcee (both combined and separately for ortho/para H2CO).
key_parameters: Emitting area = 1.4e-11 sr (from 5 sigma contour of 0.18x0.14" continuum image)
assumptions: LTE and optically thin emission (tau < 0.1 for T > 100 K)
H2CO and CH3OH emission follow the morphology of the dust crescent
Ortho-to-para ratio of H2CO = 3, A/E ratio of CH3OH = 1, N_H2 = 1.6e22 cm^-2 at 60 au

recipe.goal: Non-LTE excitation analysis of line ratios using RADEX
recipe.method: Compute non-LTE line ratios across a grid of kinetic temperatures and H2 densities using RADEX and compare with observed line ratios.
key_parameters: Molecular column density = 10^14 cm^-2, H2 density ~ 10^6 - 10^8 cm^-3
assumptions: Collisional rate coefficients from LAMDA database

recipe.goal: Physical-chemical DALI modeling of disk temperature structure and line ratios
recipe.method: Run 2D axisymmetric DALI models with varying dust surface densities between 60 and 80 au for settled and full dust columns, compute gas and dust temperatures, parametrize molecular abundance layers, and raytrace lines to compare line ratios with RADEX and observations.
key_parameters: Sigma_60au,gas = 0.25 g cm^-2; Sigma_60au,dust = 0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 5.0 g cm^-2 between 60 and 80 au; settling parameter chi = 0.1 (settled) or 0.2 (full); h_c = 0.14, psi = 0.22
Parametrized abundance = 10^-7 and 10^-9 where A_V > 1, r > 60 au, and T_dust > T_subl (66 K for H2CO, 100 K for CH3OH); 10^-12 elsewhere
assumptions: Axisymmetric Gaussian vertical density structure; step-function molecular abundances governed by sublimation temperature and UV shielding (A_V > 1)

score_reason: Raw data are publicly identifiable via ALMA project code 2017.1.00834.S, all measured integrated line fluxes and spectroscopic constants are tabulated in Table 1, and the emitting area (1.4e-11 sr) and physical assumptions for the rotational diagrams and RADEX/DALI models are explicitly stated. Minor deductions for delegating calibration to Ohashi et al. (2020) and not specifying exact Keplerian mask geometry or partition function tables.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2017.1.00834.S) is public, the imaging and spectral extraction recipe is straightforward (uvcontsub + tclean natural weighting + Keplerian masking), and the main scientific results are quantitative (13 integrated line fluxes in Table 1, rotational temperatures, column densities, and the H2CO/CH3OH ratio).
